{"code": "import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv('/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/trial.csv')

# Step 1: Exclude rows where biomarker_baseline == -999
# This is a sentinel, not a real value
print(f"Excluding {df[df['biomarker_baseline'] == -999].shape[0]} rows with biomarker_baseline == -999")

df_filtered = df[df['biomarker_baseline'] != -999].copy()

# Step 2: Deduplicate on patient_id, keeping highest sample_seq
# There are 800 unique patient_id values, but 848 rows → 48 duplicates
# We keep the highest sample_seq for each patient
print(f"Before deduplication: {df_filtered.shape[0]} rows")
df_dedup = df_filtered.loc[df_filtered.groupby('patient_id')['sample_seq'].idxmax()]
print(f"After deduplication: {df_dedup.shape[0]} rows")

# Verify: all patient_id are now unique
assert df_dedup['patient_id'].nunique() == df_dedup.shape[0], "Patient_id not unique after deduplication"

# Step 3: Check arm assignment in relation to severity (confounding)
# The data dictionary says: treatment was not randomised — clinicians gave treatment to sicker patients
# So we must check if arms are balanced by severity
print("\nCross-tabulation of arm vs severity:")
print(pd.crosstab(df_dedup['arm'], df_dedup['severity']))"}
